sourceCoverage.rationale: Twelve approximate source cues span introductory REA scope, five-step method, business examples, sponsor, targeted tools, recurring workflows, expert material and creator limitations; no certified listen-through is asserted.

supportingArgument.rationale: The article analyzes observations and creator-proposed methods using the original video and official REA repository only for bounded project scope; no independent feature or outcome claims are elevated.

evidenceRoles.rationale: Creator video claims, commercial sponsor presentation, official repository scope, machine transcript navigation and original GhostMesh editorial reasoning are explicitly separated.

counterargument.rationale: A convincing reconstructed interface can fail hidden backend, exception, security and operational conditions; a coherent expert persona cannot be assumed to recover situated judgment.

tradeoffs.rationale: The piece weighs speed of learning and narrow capability reconstruction against hidden dependencies, representativeness, exception handling, maintenance, decision rights and ownership.

falsifiability.rationale: The bounded qualification proposes real inputs and expected outputs, at least one exception and stop condition, comparison against competent human execution and documentation of unknowns.

originalSynthesis.rationale: The four-stage ladder distinguishes observation, inference, reproduction and validation, with authority treated as a separate decision beyond passing tests.

performance.rationale: No REA application reproduction, business performance improvement, Claude workflow reliability or expert-decision equivalence was measured; all remain unverified.

economics.rationale: Low implementation cost may improve learning and experimentation but does not eliminate discovery, validation, operational maintenance or the value of relationships and trust.

threatGovernance.rationale: Private retained audio/transcription hashes were independently checked; public page excludes raw source aids and explicitly limits claims and permission to act.
